doc.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

title: First gigs, dance repertoire and bebop contrafacts
summary: Dance tunes like 'How High the Moon' and learning bebop heads alongside the standards they came from.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: What would the song list have been like? And do you recall how much money you first made? Your first gig? Your first paying gig?

Oh this was amazing. Because back in those days they were dancing, social dancing. When you play for a dance, you know there’s social dancing, we played “Out of Nowhere,” we played “Caravan,” we would play, for instance we would play “How High the Moon” but then we discovered that Charlie Parker wrote a tune on “How High the Moon” and he called it “Ornithology.” So at the same time as I was playing these tunes I

would go home with this other group, you know we’d practice with this other group at school. Not go home, I’d go to school. And the other group was playing “Ornithology” and “Hot House” and “Donna Lee.” And I discovered that it was the same as those standards they was playing at the dances. So we would play these tunes but then I would play the bebop tunes and they would play the traditional Cole Porter, Rogers & Hart melody, and we would play the bebop tunes along with them. You know that’s how, we learned them together. We learned the bebop and we learned the original tunes together. A contrafact. Today they call it a contrafact.
